takeaway: Inverse-vol sizing cuts drawdowns in stress (2008 S&P -37%->-21%), improves risk-adjusted ratios 15-50%. Caveat: some studies find no consistent edge across all markets; best with capped leverage + smoothed vol forecasts. -> idea vol-targeting.

Lopez de Prado: triple-barrier = volatility-scaled TP/SL/time labels; meta-labeling separates side (direction) from size, trained on the primary model's TP/FP to filter false positives and size bets. Event-sampling + triple-barrier + meta-labeling together improve strategy performance. -> ideas triple-barrier, meta-labeling.

30d relative-strength momentum persists ~7d in crypto; long-only top-quintile + trend overlay cut max DD 75%->45% and raised return vs BTC. High market-wide correlation is the main risk. arXiv:2512.08124 uses a NN to rank assets for long-only crypto — very close to our setup, worth a deep read. -> idea xsec-momentum.

topic: long-only crypto ranking (NN) — arXiv:2512.08124 full read
takeaway: NN ranks assets; features = last return, volatility, Sharpe, return-rank-correlation over 80d; retrain every 10d; rank^2 weighting concentrates on winners (best Sharpe 1.01, 64% ann.); weight-decay alpha=0.7 cuts churn. BUT max drawdown 77.4%, NO drawdown/vol control, and it 'drops at the end of the bearish market' — cross-sectional ranking ALONE does not survive bear markets. For us it is a SELECTION/SIZING refinement (prefer/size by relative rank among our entry candidates), not a bear defense; our trend filter + vol targeting + 25% mandate supply the defense the paper lacks. rank^2 sizing is worth an experiment on top of our gates.

Overlapping labels are non-IID -> double-count info -> overfitting + poor out-of-sample (exactly what our sealed 2026 just flagged for the new champion). Fix: instantaneous uniqueness of label i at t = 1/c_t (c_t=concurrent labels); average over the label's lifespan = its sample weight; down-weight redundant overlapping samples in the loss (BCE weight). Alt: sequential bootstrap / bagging with max_samples=avg uniqueness. Training-only change; A/B on/off via the loop.

topic: ensemble / bagging of NNs for variance reduction & generalization
takeaway: Bagging NNs = train N on seed/bootstrap-varied data, average predictions -> primarily reduces VARIANCE -> lower generalization error, less volatile returns, higher risk-return in financial time series. Directly targets our two open problems: year-to-year consistency (the law) and the sealed-2026 generalization gap that uniqueness did NOT close. Cost for us: N x train time per iteration (~40min -> ~120min at N=3). Implementation: ensemble param -> train N seed-varied nets, average sigmoid probs at infer.export before the band. A/B ensemble 1 vs 3.

topic: purged & embargoed cross-validation (Lopez de Prado ch.7)
takeaway: PURGE: drop train samples whose label-formation window overlaps the val range. EMBARGO: also drop a buffer of bars right after the val boundary. Prevents leakage that inflates validation and hurts out-of-sample. For us: our zigzag oracle labels are computed over the WHOLE series, so train bars near the split can 'know' post-split prices via pivots -> a subtle leak that could inflate our val-based band/selection and widen the sealed-2026 gap. Current pooled.py split already leaves a +window gap; a larger explicit embargo + purging boundary samples would tighten it. Complementary (does NOT touch the oracle).

topic: market breadth as an absolute risk-off regime filter (% of universe in uptrend)
takeaway: Percent of index members above a moving average is a canonical breadth/risk-off REGIME filter: >50% supports long exposure; PERSISTENT readings <~40% mean rallies are narrow and prone to failure (risk-off); extremes <20% = washed out. It fires ahead of broad market peaks and is used to rotate OUT of risk. Maps directly to our open problem: 2022 is a BROAD bear where the per-symbol trend filter still lets lone bounces in. Our causal __trend bit per coin is analogous to 'in an uptrend'; universe breadth = fraction of the 14 coins with trend=1. An ABSOLUTE gate (flatten the whole book when breadth < K) is a market-wide regime switch, DISTINCT from the rejected cross-sectional (relative) momentum gate which only reranks names and never de-risks. -> idea market-breadth-gate (original synthesis for our universe).

title: A hidden return engine: harnessing crypto's volatility through rebalancing
why: Volatility harvesting applied to crypto: a rebalanced basket earns FROM volatility even when price ends where it started. Long-only and no shorting, so it fits our mandate exactly, and it targets the flat years where our worst year lives.
caveat: The article's own caveat is the one that matters here: commissions eat the premium. At 15m bars with a 0.30% round trip, rebalancing must be daily or weekly, never per-bar.

title: From volatility drag to rebalancing lift: lessons from Shannon's demon
why: The mechanism in its original form (Shannon, 1961): rebalancing a volatile asset against cash converts variance into return in a market that goes nowhere. This is the cleanest statement of why a sideways year need not be a zero year.

title: Regime- and tail-dependent performance of CVaR-based portfolio strategies in cryptocurrencies (2026)
why: Our selection law IS a tail measure - the worst calendar year - but we reach it indirectly by gridding a risk layer. This paper evaluates regime-dependent CVaR optimisation on crypto over 2018-2025, i.e. optimising the tail natively.

title: Regime switching forecasting for cryptocurrencies
why: Uses three regimes - low volatility, high volatility, distress - to set the invested share. Our gate is binary (uptrend or flat), which is precisely the design that pins the worst year near zero.

title: Innovative reward functions in reinforcement learning models for crypto trading (2026)
why: Asymmetric market-conditional objectives: different behaviour rewarded per regime rather than one objective everywhere. Relevant because our labels are regime-blind - the oracle defines a good trade the same way in 2021 and in 2022.

title: Optimal investment under transaction costs: a threshold rebalanced portfolio approach
why: Under PROPORTIONAL transaction costs the optimal rebalancing rule is MOVE-based (tolerance bands), not time-based. Our 0.30% round trip is exactly proportional, so this corrected the design of the volatility-harvesting test before it was built.

title: Maximizing the rebalancing premium
why: States the condition the premium actually depends on: DISPERSION between assets, not volatility alone. If assets are highly correlated, positions do not outgrow one another and there is little to harvest. This is the caveat that turned out to be decisive for a crypto-only basket.

title: Volatility harvesting: from theory to practice
why: The gap between the Shannon thought experiment and a book that pays fees and holds correlated assets.

title: How do you limit drawdown using the Kelly formula (Chan)
why: Practitioner treatment of the exact question P06 asks: how large a position a strategy may carry given a maximum-drawdown limit. Relevant because our mandate is a HARD 25% and our current drawdowns are 2.7-10%, i.e. we are far below any binding constraint.

title: The Kelly growth-optimal strategy with a stop-loss rule
why: Growth-optimal sizing when a stop rule is present, which is our case (stop_loss 0.08, trail_stop 0.12). Also the source of the standard result that HALF-Kelly cuts volatility by about three quarters while giving up only a quarter of the growth - so the return/risk curve is convex and the interesting region is well below the optimum.

title: Beware of excessive leverage: Kelly and optimal f
why: The other side of the trade, and the reason P06 must be reported as a curve: past the optimum, more size REDUCES growth as well as raising risk. Guards against reading 'deploy more' as 'deploy as much as possible'.

title: Data labelling methods (triple-barrier, meta-labeling)
why: The triple-barrier method labels an entry by which barrier the PATH hits first - profit-take, stop, or time - so a positive label means the trade survives the risk machinery, not merely that price ended higher. Our oracle labels ignore the path entirely, yet the shipped book exits through stops and trails.

title: Trend-scanning labeling
why: Variable-horizon labels: test multiple forward windows per observation and label by the most statistically significant trend, letting the data pick each bar's horizon. Relevant to A53 - a regime-adaptive alternative to our fixed zigzag threshold.
